reason: The returning clouds could join the dense gas disk and address whether expelled gas can make stars.
expectation: I expect the clouds to mix with the disk and perhaps form new stars, though some intermediate gathering may be needed.

alternatives.reason: Feeding the black hole addresses the other goal, but I want to follow the star-forming path first.

effect: Returning gas formed stars in the central disk, completing that goal; I will follow its other route toward the black hole.
reaction: Satisfying to see the outward journey lead back to star formation.
reason: The remaining goal asks whether returning gas can feed the dark centre.
expectation: I expect some returning gas to enter the black hole's surrounding flow and potentially feed it.

alternatives.reason: The outward clouds could also interact with thin gas, but the black hole route addresses the remaining goal directly.

effect: The returning gas also replenished the black hole's external disk, completing the second goal.
reaction: Satisfying to see the outflow feed the same central source again.

mostWorthwhile.text: Returning the clouds to the black hole was worthwhile because it closed the loop between the outflow and renewed central light.

leastWorthwhile.text: The two choices were direct routes to their named goals, so neither required much deliberation.

surprise.text: The returning material could form stars as well as feed the central disk; the outflow had not ended either possibility.

arbitrary.text: Neither chosen action felt arbitrary: each had a clear destination and purpose.

continue.text: I would continue to see where the recycled material goes next, though I would hope for more meaningful choices.
